title: Peanut butter flapjacks
subtitle: oat bars enriched with peanut butter and golden syrup
excerpt: Peanut butter flapjacks swap some of the butter in a standard flapjack for smooth or crunchy peanut butter, which deepens the flavour and adds a slight chew to the finished bar. They are made in one pan, pressed into a tin, and baked until golden. The key is not to overbake: flapjacks firm up considerably as they cool, and bars that look underdone in the oven will set to the right chewy consistency once cold.
sourceNotes: The peanut butter flapjack is a British home-baking variation on the classic flapjack (oat bar), itself documented in British cookery books from the mid-20th century. The substitution of some butter for peanut butter is a common home-kitchen adaptation that circulated widely in the 1990s and 2000s through Women's Institute and charity cookery collections. The technique is identical to the standard British flapjack, itself a descendant of the parkin and oat-cake traditions of northern England.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a single layer then transfer to a container. Defrost at room temperature for 1 hour.
recipe.batchNotes: Use a larger tin and increase bake time by 3 to 5 minutes for a double batch.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in an airtight tin for up to 1 week.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional; 20 to 22 minutes until the edges are golden and the centre looks set but still slightly soft

content.text: Peanut butter flapjacks are made by melting the fats and sweeteners together in a saucepan, stirring in the oats, then pressing into a tin and baking. The whole process takes about 15 minutes to prepare. The trickiest part is the timing: pull the tin from the oven when the edges are just golden and the centre still looks slightly underdone. The bars firm up as they cool; a flapjack that looks right in the oven will be too hard once cold.

Heat the oven to 170°C (conventional). Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper. Put {{unsalted-butter}}, {{peanut-butter}}, {{golden-syrup}}, and {{light-brown-sugar}} in a medium saucepan over a low heat. Stir until the butter melts and the mixture is smooth. Remove from the heat and stir in {{vanilla-extract}} and {{sea-salt-fine}}.
Add the oats and press into the tin

Tip {{rolled-oats}} into the pan and stir well until every oat is coated. Scrape into the lined tin and press level with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass. Press firmly and evenly, especially into the corners.

Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until the edges are turning golden and pulling away from the sides of the tin. The centre will still look a little soft; this is correct. Remove from the oven and mark out 16 bars immediately with a sharp knife while still warm; they set firmly as they cool and are very difficult to cut neatly once cold. Leave in the tin on a wire rack for at least 1 hour before removing.
